title: Human Expert Evaluation of Agentic AI for EO, form F18
description:
Thank you for helping us evaluate the performance of different LLMs in Agentic AI frameworks for EO!

WHAT THIS IS
We built a benchmark to test the performance of different LLMs in agentic settings. This evaluation form is to compare the answers given by these LLMs when answering a question using different tools related to the agentic framework that we built - including different EO endpoints (Copernicus/Sentinel, Landsat), ERA5 climate data, EO Dashboard narratives, ESA science strategy documents, GIS analysis and scientific literature search.

You will be given 8 questions, and for each question you see every anonymous answer that assistant actually produced for it -- usually several, occasionally just one if only one assistant answered that particular question.

WHAT YOU DO
(About 41 minutes for this form -- your progress is saved in this browser, so it's fine to do this over more than one sitting.) The form will guide you through it, but for every question you will
1. Rate how relevant and realistic the question is for EO users.
2. Score the accuracy of each answer shown.
3. If there's more than one answer, rank them all from best to worst (skip this step when only one answer is shown -- there's nothing to compare it to).

HOW TO JUDGE ACCURACY
Judge scientific and domain correctness, and whether the answer addresses every part of the question. A minority of answers (marked "▣ image" next to the answer letter) include the actual image the assistant looked at -- check the description against it directly. For every other answer you cannot open the files or images it says it produced: treat claims that you find implausible or unsupported as errors. Do not reward length or formatting. If you cannot judge a question, say so in the comment field and give your best estimate.

Answers were produced automatically and may contain errors. Local file paths were removed from the answers. Long answers are collapsed by default — click an answer to expand it.

PRIVACY
Your name is recorded so we can follow up if needed, and is not shown to other experts. Responses are used only for the research evaluation of this benchmark and are reported in aggregate. Participation is voluntary; you can stop at any time by closing the page.

profile_fields.title: Name
profile_fields.help: So we know who a response came from. Not shown to other experts.

profile_fields.title: How would you rate your Earth Observation expertise?
Which areas are you experienced in?
choices: Climate and atmospheric data (ERA5, trace gases)

profile_fields.title: Consent
choices: I agree that my responses are used for the research evaluation of this benchmark.

relevance.title: How relevant and realistic is this question for EO users (researchers, analysts, practitioners)?
relevance.help: 1 = not relevant or unrealistic; 3 = plausible but marginal or somewhat artificial; 5 = highly relevant and realistic.

accuracy.title: Accuracy: how correct and complete is each answer?
accuracy.help: 1 = incorrect or unusable; 2 = mostly incorrect or major omissions; 3 = partially correct or incomplete; 4 = mostly correct, minor issues; 5 = correct and complete. Equal scores are allowed.

ranking.title: Ranking: order all answers from best to worst.
ranking.help: Drag, or use the arrows, to put the best answer at the top and the worst at the bottom. Ties are not allowed.

familiarity.title: How familiar are you with the topic of this question?

comment.title: Comment (optional)
comment.help: For example: an error you spotted, why a question is not relevant, or that you could not judge it.

items.question: Search for recent arXiv papers on SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) flood mapping and inundation detection published since January 2022.

answers.text:
Here are 10 recent papers on SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) flood mapping and inundation detection published since January 2022:

1. Attentive Dual Stream Siamese U-net for Flood Detection on Multi-temporal Sentinel-1 Data
• Authors: Ritu Yadav, Andrea Nascetti, Yifang Ban
• Abstract: This paper proposes a flood detection network using bi-temporal SAR acquisitions. The network employs an encoder-decoder architecture with two Siamese encoders for pre- and post-flood images. Attention blocks are used to enhance feature maps, improving the accuracy of flood detection. The network is evaluated on the Sen1Flood11 benchmark dataset and outperforms existing uni-temporal methods by 6% IOU.
• Categories: cs.CV, eess.IV
• Published: 2022-04-20
• URL: arXiv:2204.09387 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.09387v1)

2. Remote Sensing Imagery for Flood Detection: Exploration of Augmentation Strategies
• Authors: Vladyslav Polushko, Damjan Hatic, Ronald Rösch, Thomas Mätz, Markus Rauhut, Andreas Weinmann
• Abstract: This study explores various augmentation strategies for training deep neural networks to detect floods in RGB imagery using the BlessemFlood21 dataset. The goal is to refine the training process of state-of-the-art deep learning segmentation networks for more accurate flood detection.
• Categories: cs.CV, eess.IV
• Published: 2025-04-28
• URL: arXiv:2504.20203 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.20203v1)

3. Portraying the Need for Temporal Data in Flood Detection via Sentinel-1
• Authors: Xavier Bou, Thibaud Ehret, Rafael Grompone von Gioi, Jeremy Anger
• Abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of existing flood detection datasets by extending the MMFlood dataset to include multi-date Sentinel-1 observations. It reframes flood detection as a temporal anomaly detection problem and provides a baseline method inspired by the ViBe video change detector.
• Categories: cs.CV, eess.IV
• Published: 2024-03-06
• URL: arXiv:2403.03671 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.03671v1)

4. Scalable Surface Water Mapping up to Fine-scale using Geometric Features of Water from Topographic Airborne LiDAR Data
• Authors: Hunsoo Song, Jinha Jung
• Abstract: This paper proposes a method for scalable surface water mapping using geometric features of water from airborne LiDAR data. The method focuses on the geometric characteristics of water rather than its reflectance properties, eliminating the need for training labels or site-specific parameter tuning.
• Categories: cs.CV, eess.IV
• Published: 2023-01-16
• URL: arXiv:2301.06567 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.06567v2)

5. AI Driven Water Segmentation with Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Flood Monitoring
• Authors: Sanjida Afrin Mou, Tasfia Noor Chowdhury, Adib Ibn Mannan, Sadia Nourin Mim, Lubana Tarannum, Tasrin Noman, Jamal Uddin Ahamed
• Abstract: This study compares the performance of UNet, ResNet, and DeepLabv3 for pixel-wise water segmentation to aid in flood detection. The models are tested on a new dataset that augments benchmark datasets with flood-specific images, providing insights into their applicability in different scenarios.
• Categories: cs.CV, cs.AI, cs.LG, eess.IV
• Published: 2025-01-14
• URL: arXiv:2501.08266 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.08266v1)

6. BlessemFlood21: Advancing Flood Analysis with a High-Resolution Georeferenced Dataset for Humanitarian Aid Support
• Authors: Vladyslav Polushko

1. Advanced Flood Prediction with Physics-Guided Deep Learning: Combining UNet, FNO, and SAR/Optical Imagery (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06524v1)
Authors: Tewodros Syum Gebre, Jagrati Talreja, Leila Hashemi-Beni
Published: June 2, 2026
Categories: Computer Vision (eess.IV, cs.CV, cs.LG)
Summary: Proposes a physics-guided deep learning framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, and DEM-derived terrain features with hydrodynamic constraints (shallow water equations). Demonstrates physically coherent flood predictions with low residuals and mass imbalance (<2.1%).

Authors: Sebastian Fieldhouse, Roberto Del Prete, Gabriele Daga, et al.

Categories: Computer Vision (eess.IV, cs.CE, cs.ET)
Summary: Introduces the first Online SAR Processor (OSP), an online image-formation framework that processes SAR data line-by-line during acquisition. Achieves 70× lower latency and 130× lower memory use compared to traditional baselines. Demonstrates flood-mapping capabilities while maintaining high focusing quality.

Authors: Siddharth Kothari, Srinivasan Murali, Sankalp Kothari, et al.

I found several recent papers on SAR-based flood mapping and inundation detection published since January 2022. The research generally falls into three categories: benchmark datasets, methodological evaluations/reviews, and operational systems.

1. Benchmark Datasets & Deep Learning
Several papers focus on creating large-scale datasets to improve deep learning models for flood segmentation:
• UrbanSARFloods (2024): A Sentinel-1 SLC-based benchmark dataset specifically targeting the challenge of urban flood mapping, which is often more difficult than open-area mapping due to complex geometry (arXiv:2406.04111).
• Kuro Siwo (2023): A massive global multi-temporal dataset covering 43 flood events and mapping 33 billion $m^2$ of flooded areas, designed to promote research on both phase and amplitude information (arXiv:2311.12056).
• Adversarial Robustness (2025): A study on the robustness of U-Net models for inland water body segmentation, specifically examining how manual annotation errors (label noise) affect performance (arXiv:2505.01884).

2. Methodological Evaluations & Reviews
These papers analyze the "how" and "why" of SAR flood mapping:
• Preprocessing & Hyperparameters (2025): An evaluation of how speckle noise reduction and hyperparameter tuning impact flood extent and water depth estimation, suggesting that an ensemble approach is better than a single configuration (arXiv:2510.11305).
• Urban Flood Mapping Review (2024): A comprehensive review of characteristics, approaches, and datasets for urban flooding, highlighting the potential of Polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) and the need for more open-access urban datasets (arXiv:2411.04153).
• Daily High-Resolution Observations (2022): Research on fusing high-spatial/low-temporal resolution data (Sentinel-1/2) with low-spatial/high-temporal data (NASA SMAP/GPM) using CNNs to achieve daily inundation maps (arXiv:2208.09135).

3. Operational Systems & Real-time Processing
• Copernicus GFM (2023): A paper on the Global Flood Monitoring system, which uses an ensemble of three independent algorithms to provide near-real-time flood extent masks and likelihood products (arXiv:2304.12488).
• Online SAR Processor (2026 - Pre-print/Future): A novel framework using state-space models to produce focused SAR images line-by-line during acquisition, significantly reducing latency for downstream tasks like flood mapping (arXiv:2605.10340).
